basis: Paris Time Machine blocks and R40 stone streets; high street wall and interior court.
Guangzhou historical lanes and port constraints from frozen cards; narrow deep plan and side passages are a reconstruction.
New York and Jersey City period plans record differentiated blocks and rail yards; masonry and timber proportions are inferred.
Rio 1900 plan sets roads, openings, shore and slopes; low block perimeter and courtyard massing are inferred.

The URA Kampong Glam trail dates the early style to 1840–1900 and records typical frontages of 4–6 m and depths of at least two to three times the width (https://www.roots.gov.sg/-/media/Roots/Files/ura-kampong-glam-trail/urakampongglamtrail19_brochure.pdf). URA documents two- to three-storey party-wall rows, pitched clay tile roofs, rear courts and covered street arcades (https://www.ura.gov.sg/conservation/conservation-resources/understanding-the-shophouse/). NLB documents timber spans and open airwells in the historic rows (https://biblioasia.nlb.gov.sg/all-sections/vol-2-issue2-jul-2006-ethnic-enclave-urban-settlement/). Model depths are a representative 12–18 m band. Roof geometry, eave height, exact street setback, wall and tile colours, and relative airwell dimensions are inferred for the Kit.
